FACT_ID: sec03-R01 | anchor: A01
Reaction distance is traveled from seeing danger until stepping on the brake, whereas braking distance is traveled from applying the brakes until stopping and becomes much longer on wet, icy, or gravel roads [A01].
Why it matters: group stopping distance; difficulty medium; prereq sec03-F09; confusables sec03-F09, sec03-F10
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-vt-class-std:vermont-department-of-motor-vehicles-age:handbook:pdf-0027]

FACT_ID: sec03-R02 | anchor: A01
The signal law is written as a distance of not less than one hundred feet, while the practical habit is counted as three to five seconds before the turn or lane change [A01].
Why it matters: group signals; difficulty low; prereq sec03-F12; confusables sec03-F12, sec03-F13
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-vt-class-std:vermont-department-of-motor-vehicles-age:handbook:pdf-0027]

FACT_ID: sec03-R03 | anchor: A02
A left turn search runs right, front, left, while a right turn search runs left, front, right and then quickly left again [A02].
Why it matters: group turn procedures; difficulty high; prereq sec03-F19; confusables sec03-F19, sec03-F21
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-vt-class-std:vermont-department-of-motor-vehicles-age:handbook:pdf-0028]

FACT_ID: sec03-R04 | anchor: A01
A left turn sets up within one foot of the centerline, whereas a right turn sets up about three feet from the right edge of the road [A01] [A02].
Why it matters: group turn procedures; difficulty medium; prereq sec03-F16; confusables sec03-F16, sec03-F20
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-vt-class-std:vermont-department-of-motor-vehicles-age:handbook:pdf-0027]

FACT_ID: sec03-R05 | anchor: A03
Fifty miles per hour is the maximum on ordinary Vermont roads, while sixty-five miles per hour applies only on the interstate, and both are capped by whatever lower limit is posted [A03].
Why it matters: group speed limits; difficulty low; prereq sec03-F27; confusables sec03-F27, sec03-F28
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-vt-class-std:vermont-department-of-motor-vehicles-age:handbook:pdf-0029]

FACT_ID: sec03-R06 | anchor: A03
At a four way stop the rule is first to arrive goes first, and only when arrivals are simultaneous does the driver on the left yield to the driver on the right [A03].
Why it matters: group right-of-way; difficulty medium; prereq sec03-F32; confusables sec03-F32, sec03-F30
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-vt-class-std:vermont-department-of-motor-vehicles-age:handbook:pdf-0029]
